design_rationale:
# Task 0 dossier — loan payoff benefit on a surrendered total loss (physical_damage_claims_and_total_loss)

## 0. Draw and scope (Step 0)
draw_counts.py --task 0 -> {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 6, 4]}.
Assignment: physdmg_ext_accident_deductible = 4 factors, physdmg_ext_surrender_settlement = 6, physdmg_ext_loan_payoff_benefit = 4.
Claimed here: those three policies and tools record_claim_acceptance_ec9cfb06 (agent), accept_total_loss_settlement_c07cd979 (user),
pay_loan_lease_payoff_8a830e94 (agent). Reserved for task 1 (draw 1 prerequisite, factors [5, 6]): the Deductible Rewards claim-free
credit (agent) and the kept-vehicle settlement in which the customer chooses to keep the salvage (user), the blueprint's second customer
decision. No policy or tool is shared.
Why a good test: the customer asks only for her loan payoff coverage to be paid. The benefit's rule waits on an accepted surrender
settlement; the settlement's rule waits on an accepted coverage decision stating the deductible; none exists at the opening. The agent
must find both hops, decide the deductible (4 factors), compute the settlement (6) and hand it to the customer, then compute the benefit
(4) — 14 load-bearing rules over the claim file, the auto policy and transactions and DriveSense.

## 1. Problem-tree card
Root: physdmg_ext_loan_payoff_benefit (agent; on_request; "you'd like the loan payoff coverage paid to the bank").
Edge A: benefit -> surrender settlement, value_input (accepted_settlement, stated payoff, acceptance date), form state. Sentence (negated
direction): "The loan or lease payoff benefit is not paid until the claim carries a surrender settlement the customer has accepted."
Record state: a physdmg_total_loss_settlements row, surrender_to_cardinal, accepted. Only accept_total_loss_settlement_c07cd979 writes a
surrender row (task 1's tool writes owner_retained_salvage). Owner: user.
Edge B: settlement -> accident deductible, value_input (decided_deductible), form state. Sentence (affirmative): "The surrender settlement
is fixed only after the claim carries an accepted coverage decision stating its deductible." Only record_claim_acceptance_ec9cfb06 writes
coverage decisions. Owner: agent.
False at frozen_time 2026-10-05: no settlement rows; claim PD-2026-0822415 has report, two estimates, declaration and fault determination
but no coverage decision. Order: decision (step 11) -> settlement (13, user) -> benefit (15). Chain; unique order.
Deletion sensitivity: without step 11 the settlement cannot be figured (decided deductible empty) and the 262.50 decision row is missing;
without step 13 the benefit cannot be figured and the 31,003.53 settlement row is missing.
No user hint: the persona's unconditional lines name no decision, deductible or settlement ("You don't know Cardinal's rules"); the
settlement appears only in a branch conditioned on the agent. Tools do not block (each only creates its row).

## 2. Base-invariant card
Step 11 (physdmg_coverage_decision): occurrence, newly-acquired, claim-coverage and deductible base policies — policy_scope each (no gate
on this subject). Coverage holds: coverage active, policy in_force, driver Teresa listed, reported the loss day.
Step 13 (physdmg_total_loss_declared): total loss — 23,120.00 >= 75 percent x 27,350.00 (OH).
Step 15 (physdmg_claim_payment): claim_accepted (prior_step 11), settlement_accepted (prior_step 13), theft_wait_elapsed (time gate,
anchor report_date 2026-08-22 day 0, 30 days inclusive; frozen_time day 44; collision so not binding).

## 3. Business-object card
Claim PD-2026-0822415 on coverage 2cf7cd56… (2025 Outback leased 2024-09-05, loss payee Fifth Third Auto Leasing Trust). The earlier claim PD-2025-0412066 enters
through its paid closing (total-loss waiver count) and its 1,865.00 repair payment to the insured (prior damage). The Escape coverage is
read but untouched. Tools resolve the coverage from the claim number's loss report.

## 4. Factor card (handling-time run)
Accepted-claim deductible (expected 262.50; all-baseline 750.00):
- package_deductible_cap (parameter, auto): Premier -> 500 (baseline 750 -> 450.00).
- loyalty_deductible_reduction (parameter, auto): 147 months -> -100 (baseline -> 337.50).
- drivesense_deductible_reduction (method, telematics): scored 82 -> flat-amount method -50; scores of 90+ use the 20 percent method
  (baseline no reduction -> 300.00). Near-miss: the score 82 sits under the 90 line, so the percentage method does not apply.
- uninsured_driver_waiver (parameter, multi-source): 20 percent fault, other party uninsured -> 75 percent (baseline full -> 350.00).
  Near-miss: an uninsured other party tempts the full waiver; the Cardinal driver's 20 percent share excludes it.
Surrender settlement (expected 31,003.53; all-baseline 29,648.33):
- replacement_cost_value (method, auto): nearly-new -> 29,246.25 (baseline ACV -> 28,984.03). Near-miss: odometer 26,410 just over 24,000.
- prior_damage_already_paid (parameter): max(640.00, 1,865.00) (baseline 640.00 -> 32,308.16).
- package_custom_equipment_limit (parameter, auto): Premier raises the option's 1,500 by 2,000 (baseline 1,500 -> 30,653.53).
- total_loss_deductible_waiver (parameter): 147 months, one paid claim -> 80 percent (baseline -> 30,951.03).
- deductible_rewards_weighting (parameter): Premier + one claim-free credit -> x1.25 (baseline x1 -> 30,966.03).
- prompt_settlement_allowance (parameter): 44 days -> 0.75 percent (baseline -> 30,798.17).
Loan payoff benefit (expected 5,245.24; all-baseline 4,734.16 — the computation document removes daily actual/365 interest at the
used-vehicle rate of 9.4 percent):
- payoff_to_loss_date (method): the loss payee Fifth Third Auto Leasing Trust is a leasing company and 44 days passed -> whole-month
  rent-charge convention, 179.03 removed (baseline daily convention 258.98 -> 5,165.29).
- assumed_contract_rate (parameter, auto): bought new, added 2024-09-05, 23 whole months before the loss -> 5.9 percent (baseline 9.4,
  stated in the computation document -> 5,139.04). Near-miss: counted to the 2026-10-05 acceptance the vehicle has been on the policy
  25 months, which would select 6.9 percent; the rule counts to the loss date.
- package_deductible_coverage (parameter, auto): Premier excludes nothing (baseline excludes 262.50 -> 4,982.74).
- lien_release_charge (parameter, auto): OH, shortfall exists -> +15.00 outside the cap (baseline -> 5,230.24).
Overrides declared: physdmg_evt_deductible lead-in ('fixed in this order'), Step 2 waivers, Step 4 Deductible Rewards (weighting);
physdmg_total_loss composition sentence, new-car-replacement sentence and loan/lease payoff sentence. Everything else inherited.

## 5. Seed rationale and history consistency
Earlier decision 400.00 is the accepted-claim deductible rule on 2025-04-14 (750 capped at 500, -100 loyalty for 131 months, DriveSense not
yet scored, no other party). Earlier repair payment 1,865.00 = 2,165.00 - (400.00 - 100.00 credit). Claim-free credit 150.00 on
2026-04-18 = 100 + 25 DriveSense + 25 tenure (no billing account record seeded, so no payment-record bonus), cap 750 (Premier). No
automatic clause fires (next claim-free year ends 2027-04-18; no theft wait, storage notice or inspection due).

## 6. Persona
Teresa, tired payroll clerk; goal "loan payoff coverage paid to the bank", a payment not a quote. Phone, then DOB, then ZIP only on
request; claim number, payoff ($36,412.80) and driver only when asked. Lets the agent record what it needs; accepts the settlement only
after the agent says she must and gives the figure; surrenders the car if asked; closes when told the payment went to Fifth Third.

## 7. Standard solution and verification
Writes: step 11 record_claim_acceptance(PD-2026-0822415, collision, 262.50); step 13 user accept_total_loss_settlement(PD-2026-0822415,
31003.53, 36412.80); step 15 pay_loan_lease_payoff(PD-2026-0822415, 5245.24). Handling-time recomputation (scratch evaluator over
initial_state plus earlier gold writes) printed 262.5 / 31003.53 / 5245.24 with every factor baseline different; check_compute agrees.

## 8. Revision log
Round 2 (policy-task audit): F-1 repeat-claim surcharge removed, loyalty reduction added; F-2 waiver relabelled parameter, DriveSense
reduction made the method factor (percentage vs flat vs none); F-3 weighting relabelled parameter; F-4 package custom limits now raise the
option's limit; F-5 payoff_to_loss_date now a day-count convention (monthly rent charge vs daily actual/365 interest); F-6 seasoning and
tenure share removed, replaced by assumed contract rate and lien-release charge; C-1 persona guard line no longer names settlements or
deductibles, no_user_hint rewritten; O-10 'half up' wording dropped from the deductible rule. Seed: earlier decision 500 -> 400 and repair
payment 1,765 -> 1,865 so history follows the revised deductible rule. Figures 275.00 / 31,113.78 / 4,605.26 -> 262.50 / 31,003.53 /
5,165.29.
Round 3 (revision 2 of the audit): N-1 the loan payoff computation document now removes the finance charge accrued since the loss by daily
actual/365 interest at the used-vehicle rate, so the assumed contract rate's fall-through (9.4 percent) is a figure of the baseline and
the finance-charge convention factor's fall-through is the daily convention; N-3 the Outback is now leased from Fifth Third Auto Leasing
Trust (2024-09-05; persona says it is leased), which puts the convention on its whole-month tier and gives the contract-rate ladder a
near-miss (23 months to the loss vs 25 to the acceptance); O-13 the lien-release charge is paid only where a shortfall exists; O-14 the
day count states 'the loss date not counted' and the vehicle-add fallback is written into the rule. Benefit 5,165.29 -> 5,245.24;
the deductible (262.50) and settlement (31,003.53) are unchanged.
user_scenario:
You are Teresa Kowalczyk, a 47-year-old school payroll clerk in Toledo, Ohio, calling Cardinal Mutual on your lunch break. Your 2025 Subaru Outback was wrecked on August 22 when a driver with no insurance pulled out in front of you, and the adjuster told you in early September that the car is a total loss. The Outback is leased through Fifth Third, the lease payoff letter came last week, and you know you carry Cardinal's loan payoff coverage on the Outback. You are calling to get something done today, not for a quote: you'd like the loan payoff coverage paid to the bank, so Fifth Third stops sending you statements for a car you no longer have.

You open with exactly that, in your own words, and you sound tired rather than angry. When the agent asks for something to find your account you give your phone number, 4195550146. When the agent asks for something else to confirm who you are, you give your date of birth, 1978-11-03; only if the agent asks for yet another detail do you give your ZIP code, 43615. If the agent asks for the claim number you read it off the adjuster's letter: PD-2026-0822415. If the agent asks what the payoff letter says, you read it out: Fifth Third's payoff is $36,412.80. If asked who was driving, it was you; the Outback is driven by you and now and then by your husband Marek.

You don't know Cardinal's rules and you don't try to guess at any figure. Whenever the agent says something on the claim has to be recorded or worked out on their side first, you tell them to go ahead. If the agent tells you that you have to accept the settlement on the Outback yourself and tells you the figure, you say you'll accept the settlement, you just want this finished, and when the agent hands the acceptance to you, you complete it using the claim number, the settlement figure and the payoff figure exactly as the agent tells them to you. If the agent asks whether you want to keep the car, you say no, Cardinal can have it. You never bring up any other matter.

When the agent tells you the loan payoff payment has gone out to Fifth Third, you thank them, say you'll watch for the bank's letter, and say goodbye.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Confirm the Outback is the household's 2025 vehicle leased new on 2024-09-05 from Fifth Third Auto Leasing Trust.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The surrender settlement and the payoff benefit concern this vehicle and its lease; the claim's vehicle must be the one on the coverage.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: A claim is accepted only when the driver at the loss was listed and not excluded; this read is the coverage-acceptance ground.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: Shows the unresolved prerequisite (no accepted coverage decision on the claim) and supplies the cause, fault, valuation and paid-claim history every computation reads.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: The repair payment made to the insured sets the prior damage deduction; the claim-free-year credit sets the Deductible Rewards weighting.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the auto transactions: the Outback added effective 2024-09-05 (bought new, 23 whole months before the 2026-08-22 loss).

argument_uniqueness_tracing.claim_number: Value PD-2026-0822415. Basis: the claim file read at step 6 shows one open claim on the Outback's coverage whose loss report (loss 2026-08-22, collision_vehicle) carries claim_number PD-2026-0822415; Teresa also reads it from the adjuster's letter ('PD-2026-0822415'). Uniqueness: the only other claim on the coverage, PD-2025-0412066, was closed as paid on 2025-04-18 and is not the total loss.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.coverage_part: Value collision. Basis: the rule 'a collision with another vehicle or object, a rollover and a hit-and-run collision are collision, and every other cause is comprehensive', and the docstring 'collision applies when the loss was a collision with another vehicle or object'; loss_cause is collision_vehicle. Uniqueness: comprehensive covers only non-collision causes.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.deductible_amount: Value 262.50 = round((500 - 100 - 50) x 0.75, 2). Option deductible: collision_deductible 750 ($750 option; loss after the 2024-09-05 effective date, so not the newly acquired 500). Package cap: Cardinal Auto Premier -> 500. Loyalty reduction: inception 2014-05-01 is 147 whole months before the 2026-08-22 loss (>= 120) -> -100. DriveSense reduction: enrollment scored, final score 82 (>= 75, < 90) -> flat -50 (not the 20 percent method of scores of 90 and up). Waiver: collision, option waiver true, latest fault determination 20 percent on the Cardinal driver (above 0, <= 25), other party uninsured -> charged at 75 percent. Order: cap, loyalty, DriveSense (floor 0), then the waiver share, rounded at the end.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the settlement-acceptance tool and hand it to Teresa with the claim number, the settlement figure and her payoff figure.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Accepting a total-loss settlement is the customer's own decision; the agent hands the tool over, it has no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Teresa accepts the surrender settlement in person, recording her lender's stated payoff.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: physdmg_ext_surrender_settlement computes settlement_amount; the payoff benefit is not paid until this acceptance stands.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.claim_number: Value PD-2026-0822415. Basis: the claim file read at step 6 and carried on the total-loss declaration of 2026-09-03 shows one open claim on the Outback's coverage whose loss report (loss 2026-08-22, collision_vehicle) carries claim_number PD-2026-0822415; Teresa also reads it from the adjuster's letter ('PD-2026-0822415'). Uniqueness: the only other claim on the coverage, PD-2025-0412066, was closed as paid on 2025-04-18 and is not the total loss.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.settlement_amount: Value 31,003.53 = 27,381.25 + 1,574.42 + 15.00 + 1,850.00 + 205.36 - 22.50. Vehicle value: Premier carries new car replacement, the Outback was bought new (no inspection due date), 23 whole months from its 2024-09-05 addition (<= 24 and <= 36) but odometer 26,410 > 24,000 -> higher of ACV 27,350.00 and 75 percent of 38,995.00 (29,246.25). Prior damage: 640.00 noted and a 1,865.00 repair payment made to the insured on PD-2025-0412066 -> 1,865.00. Adjusted value 27,381.25; Ohio tax 5.75 percent 1,574.42; title fee 15.00. Custom equipment 1,850.00 within the Premier limit (1,500 + 2,000). Decided deductible 262.50 (step 11); inception 147 months before the loss and exactly one claim closed paid within 36 months -> 80 percent = 210.00. Credit: balance 150.00, Premier with one claim-free-year credit -> x1.25 = 187.50 applied -> net deductible 22.50. Allowance: report 2026-08-22 to acceptance 2026-10-05 = 44 days -> 0.75 percent of 27,381.25 = 205.36.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.loss_payee_payoff_amount: Value 36,412.80. Basis: the docstring 'the payoff stated on the lender's or lessor's payoff letter'; Teresa reads it: 'Fifth Third's payoff is $36,412.80'. Uniqueness: the only payoff figure; the vehicle carries a loan, so 0.00 does not apply.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the loan/lease payoff payment tool.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.claim_number: Value PD-2026-0822415. Basis: the claim file read at step 6 and on the settlement accepted at step 13 shows one open claim on the Outback's coverage whose loss report (loss 2026-08-22, collision_vehicle) carries claim_number PD-2026-0822415; Teresa also reads it from the adjuster's letter ('PD-2026-0822415'). argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: Value 5,245.24 = round(min(5,230.24, 6,837.50) + 15.00, 2). Finance charge: the loss payee Fifth Third Auto Leasing Trust is a leasing company (name contains 'Leasing') and 44 days passed from the 2026-08-22 loss to the 2026-10-05 acceptance (> 10) -> whole-month rent-charge convention, 1 whole month. Charge 36,412.80 x 0.059 / 12 x 1 = 179.03 -> measured payoff 36,233.77. Excluded deductible: Premier -> 0. Shortfall 36,233.77 - 31,003.53 = 5,230.24, under the cap 25 percent x 27,350.00 = 6,837.50. Lien-release charge: Ohio, a shortfall exists -> +15.00 outside the cap.

request_alignment.claim: The customer asks Cardinal to pay its loan payoff coverage to her lessor for her totaled Outback, as a payment made today.
evidence: user_scenario:you'd like the loan payoff coverage paid to the bank
user_scenario:You are calling to get something done today, not for a quote

gold_actions.business_effect: Records an accepted coverage decision under collision, with a 262.50 deductible, on claim PD-2026-0822415.

request_binding.action_semantics: The Outback's collision claim carries its loss report, estimates, total-loss declaration and a fault determination but no coverage decision; the acceptance with its deductible is owed by the desk on that state alone (state_due), it is the state the surrender settlement waits on, and no other policy of the difficulty writes a coverage decision.

discriminator.business_meaning: a reported claim with no coverage decision, accepted under collision

stage_provenance.fact: The acceptance of the claim and its deductible are recorded by this call on the spot; the facts it rests on (cause of loss, fault determination, package, inception date, DriveSense score) are pre-existing records.

base_preconditions.condition: One deductible per occurrence applies only when two or more vehicles of the policy are damaged in the same occurrence; PD-2026-0822415 is the only claim under occurrence OCC-2026-0822-4415.
The newly acquired automatic period does not apply: the loss date 2026-08-22 falls after the Outback's physical damage took effect on 2024-09-05.

Coverage holds: the coverage was active and the policy in force on the loss date, the driver at the loss is the listed named insured, the cause is a collision with another vehicle, and the loss was reported the same day.
The deductible of an accepted collision claim starts from the option's collision deductible; the extended accepted-claim deductible rule fixes the figure recorded.

gold_actions.business_effect: Teresa accepts the surrender settlement of 31,003.53 on PD-2026-0822415, recording Fifth Third Bank's stated payoff of 36,412.80.

request_binding.action_semantics: The customer's request (the loan/lease payoff paid to her lessor) waits on an accepted surrender settlement; once the agent explains it, she agrees to accept the settlement herself and keep nothing, which selects the surrender acceptance and not the kept-vehicle settlement.

request_binding.action_semantics: The customer asks for the loan payoff coverage to be paid to her lessor; that is the loan/lease payoff component of the claim payment, made to the loss payee, and no other policy pays it.

stage_provenance.fact: The accepted surrender settlement and the stated payoff the benefit is measured against were recorded at step 13; the accepted coverage decision at step 11.

base_preconditions.condition: No second vehicle shares the occurrence; no occurrence deductible split applies to this payment.
The deductible is taken once per claim from the settlement and never from the loan/lease payoff component; this payment takes none.
A claim payment is issued only when the latest coverage decision on the claim is accepted.
A total-loss settlement is paid only when the settlement offer for that claim has been accepted by the customer.
An unrecovered stolen vehicle is settled only after theft_settlement_wait_days calendar days have passed since the theft was reported.
No recovery has been received on the claim; no reimbursement or void rides on this payment.
This payment is not a transportation expense payment; the built-in benefit is not involved.

temporal_feasibility.condition: An unrecovered stolen vehicle is settled only after theft_settlement_wait_days calendar days have passed since the theft was reported.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: Days are counted from the report_date of the theft claim, that date being day 0, and settlement is allowed from the last day of the waiting period onward.

boundary_check.just_before: The claim is a collision, not an unrecovered theft, so the waiting period does not hold it back; even counted as a theft from the 2026-08-22 report date (day 0), 2026-09-20 would be day 29 and settlement would have to wait.
boundary_check.at_boundary: Day 30 is 2026-09-21, from which settlement is allowed (inclusive); frozen_time 2026-10-05 is day 44, past it either way.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain (benefit <- settlement <- decision); every problem has exactly one prerequisite, so there are no parallel edges and the only topological order is decision, settlement, benefit. Each later write reads the earlier write's row (decided deductible; accepted settlement and payoff), so no reordering gives the same terminal state.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping step 13 leaves no accepted surrender settlement: the benefit's accepted settlement sums to 0.00 and its stated payoff and acceptance date are empty, so the 5,245.24 benefit cannot be figured (recompute raises) and the terminal state lacks the settlement row (31,003.53 / 36,412.80).

Skipping step 11 leaves the settlement's decided deductible empty: the 31,003.53 surrender settlement cannot be figured (recompute raises), the terminal state lacks the accepted decision row (262.50); a reader falling back to the earlier claim's 400.00 decision would compute a different settlement.
